evidence: app/src/routes/abilities/[name].ts:1 — the whole Abilities feature is one self-contained route directory
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:234 — the only inbound link is the spec-mandated Abilities section on the Pokémon page, an expected edit
app/src/lib/data.ts:49 — `abilities` field on ApiPokemon would be left as a harmless type leftover (no dead runtime code)
app/src/document.ts:25-29 — nav is centralized, so removing Team means one obvious link edit here
app/src/client/team-list.ts:1 — Team removal touches ~9 files (route, lib/team.ts, 3 client islands, document.client.ts, pokemon page toggle, CSS), each a small grep-able edit
removability.rationale: Abilities is nearly perfect to remove (one directory + one mandated section). Team is inherently cross-cutting, so its removal fans out over more files, but every touch point is small and discoverable.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:73 — `spriteUrl` is the single sprite source; app/src/components/partials.ts:24 is its only use, so one fix covers home, moves, abilities, types and team lists
app/src/lib/data.ts:170-189 — `cardsForPokemon` funnels three card lists through one sort/dedupe, so a card bug is fixed once

app/src/lib/api.ts:80 — `isBuildRender` guard is copy-pasted into 6 handlers (routes/moves/[name].ts:45, routes/abilities/[name].ts:35, routes/types/[name].ts:50, routes/pokemon/[name].ts:168, routes/(home).ts:18, routes/team.ts:89); forgetting it in a new route silently fetches API data at build time, which the spec forbids
app/src/client/team-toggle.ts:35 — 'Add to team'/'Team is full' strings duplicated against app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:202-205, so a copy change lands in two different mechanisms
app/src/lib/data.ts:245 — name-validation regex duplicated at app/src/lib/data.ts:351 (`validName`)
changeability.rationale: The highest-value fixes (sprite, card lists, API rules) are one obvious place. A handful of smaller fixes (copy strings, validation, effect fallback) land in two or three places because small logic was inlined instead of shared.

evidence: app/src/routes/moves/[name].ts:28-43 vs :55-70 — handler returns plain view-model props, template consumes props; a clean data/render seam repeated on every route
app/src/client/fragments.ts:13-18 — islands re-fetch server-rendered HTML instead of duplicating templates, keeping server and client rendering in one source of truth
app/src/lib/team.ts:26-39 — the cookie format is one shared module used by both server handlers (routes/team.ts:90) and the client store, with a comment saying so
app/src/client/team-toggle.ts:13 — islands talk to the server only via data-* attributes, no internals shared
app/src/lib/api.ts:80 — `isBuildRender` leaks Gracile's internal stub hostname ('gracile-static') into every route handler; centralized but each handler is coupled to the build-render concept
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:123 — `moveTables` exported from the route file though nothing imports it
coupling.rationale: Narrow interfaces and clear server/client separation throughout; the one real tangle is the build-render detection that every handler must know about.

evidence: app/src/lib/data.ts:170-189 — `cardsForPokemon` is a generic helper with ref/extra callbacks, designed exactly around the real variation (hidden-ability flag on abilities route:35-39) and reused by 3 routes
app/src/components/partials.ts:55-77 — `cardList`/`section`/`count`/`notFound` are small composable primitives reused by every page
app/src/lib/data.ts:196-232 — `getPokemonIndex` derives types/generations from aggregate endpoints instead of 1025 per-Pokémon fetches; designed around the app's real scale

app/src/routes/moves/[name].ts:45-52 vs app/src/routes/abilities/[name].ts:35-40 — the 404 route scaffolding is near-identical in four routes; adding Items means copying ~90 lines rather than calling a helper
app/src/lib/data.ts:146-152 — Card's optional `types`/`hidden` flags are mild optional-field creep but map to genuine variation
abstraction_design.rationale: The shared primitives (cards pipeline, partials, fragment fetcher) stretch well to new cases without flag parameters. The missing abstraction is a resource-route wrapper, so sibling resource pages are structural copy-paste rather than reuse.

findings.issue: The build-render guard (`isBuildRender`) must be manually repeated in every route handler (6 sites); a new route that omits it fetches live API data during the build, violating a spec constraint and breaking the 'data at request time' rule under the test harness's overlay data.
findings.suggestion: Make the transport itself build-aware — e.g. have `api()`/`apiRequired()` return empty/null when a build-render flag (set from a global or the gracile plugin) is set — so routes cannot get it wrong.

findings.issue: Team-toggle UI strings ('Add to team'/'Remove from team'/'Team is full') and the full button-state logic exist twice: in the Lit template (app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:201-206) and in client DOM code, so copy or state changes must be made in two places and can drift.
findings.suggestion: Have the client element carry the strings as data attributes rendered by the server, or make the client render the whole toggle from a single shared state object.

findings.issue: The resource-name validation regex is duplicated: inline in `getSpecies` and as `validName` (data.ts:351).
findings.suggestion: Use `validName` in `getSpecies` too (or fold all four getters into one parameterized `getResource(kind, name)`).

findings.issue: The effect fallback chain (`englishShortEffect ?? latestEnglishFlavor ?? DASH`) is duplicated in the abilities route (app/src/routes/abilities/[name].ts:24-26).
`moveTables` is exported from the route module but only used inside it; markup helpers for the moves table live in the route file instead of components/.
findings.suggestion: Move it to components/ (unexported) so routes stay thin and the components module stays the single home for shared markup.

findings.issue: `teamFromCookieHeader(request.headers.get('cookie'))` is repeated in three handlers (also pokemon/[name].ts:169), a small repeated seam for reading shared browser state.
findings.suggestion: Wrap it in a tiny `teamFromRequest(request)` helper in lib/team.ts.

findings.issue: Card sprites are computed from the numeric ID rather than read from the API-provided `front_default`, so a Pokémon whose front sprite is null can't render a placeholder and any sprite-path change (e.g. shiny sets) needs a new URL builder.
findings.suggestion: Carry the sprite URL (or its absence) on the `Card` view model, sourced from the default Pokémon's `sprites.front_default`.

summary: A well-factored Gracile app that hits the framework's current idioms: SSR file routes, plain view-model props, and thin client islands that re-fetch server fragments instead of duplicating templates. Card lists, formatting rules and API access are each centralized, so the biggest fixes land in one place. The repeated per-route scaffolding (build-render guard, 404 pattern, name validation) and a few duplicated strings are the only things a maintainer will pay for.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Delete the abilities/ route directory, remove the Abilities section (pokemon/[name].ts:234-247) and the `abilities` mapping in load() (:78-85). data.ts:49's `abilities` field is optional type cleanup; no nav, client code or shared helper needs touching.

scenarios.change: Fix the wrong-sprite bug for species whose default Pokémon has a different name
scenarios.notes: Sprites come from one function (`spriteUrl`, api.ts:73) rendered by one helper (`cardLink`, partials.ts:24), so one fix covers every list automatically. The caveat: `Card` only carries an id, so a fix that uses the Pokémon's actual `front_default` also needs plumbing through `cardsForPokemon`/`getPokemonIndex` (data.ts) — still one pipeline, 2-3 files.

scenarios.change: Add sorting by name to every list of Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: Three of the four lists are produced by `cardsForPokemon` (sort at data.ts:189); the home page's order comes from `getSpeciesList` (data.ts:113). Team must stay insertion-ordered per FEATURE.md, so it's an intentional exclusion. If 'sorting' means a user-facing control instead of default order, it becomes a route + client-island change on the home page too.

scenarios.change: Add an Items section (/items, /items/:name) shaped like Moves
scenarios.notes: All the real logic is reusable as-is: api client, format helpers, `section`/`count`/`notFound` partials, `document`, the 404 pattern. What gets copied is ~90 lines of route scaffolding (isBuildRender guard, load/validate/404 handler, document title) because there's no resource-route abstraction to hang it on. If item pages show card lists, `cardsForPokemon` works unchanged.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: `API_BASE_URL`, the cache TTL (TTL_MS:8), the concurrency limiter (MAX_CONCURRENT:9) and the media-URL builder (`spriteUrl`:73) all live in one 81-line module; no route constructs an API URL itself (verified by grep). A URL scheme or cache-policy change is a single-file edit.
